title: Unera
intro: Brand identity and stationery for an educational social network start-up entering a crowded online-learning market. Five letters, five shapes, and a palette everyone can read.
brief: Unera was entering a crowded online-education market and needed to stand out: minimal but memorable, youthful but relatable to an older audience, and clearly apart from the big corporations. The palette had to work for people with colour blindness, and the identity had to hold up in print and at exhibitions as well as on screen.
did: We reduced each letter of the name to a simple geometric form. In a row they spell the wordmark, stacked they form a monogram, and repeated they build a pattern, so one small set of shapes does the work of the whole system.

Each colour stays distinct across every type of colour blindness, keeping the shapes readable for everyone. From there we set up the core stationery, ready for the heavy correspondence the company had planned.
